title: Drinks
description: Name the drinks, and ask for one at the bar.
grammar: gender and articles, and the words for a drink
grammarNote: A drink takes un or una when you ask for one, and the noun tells you which.

explanation.summary: Drinks are nouns like any other, and the bar is where a learner first uses them. Two of them are phrases, and one of them keeps el even though it is a feminine word.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: El zumo, el vino, el refresco, el ponche and el café con leche are masculine. La cerveza, la limonada, la infusión and la horchata are feminine. El agua con gas is the exception that proves the rule: agua is feminine, but a stressed final -a takes el, exactly like el agua and el agua mineral.

sections.heading: At the bar
sections.body: You ask for a drink with un or una and the name of the drink: un zumo, una cerveza, un café con leche. A cold drink is un zumo frío, and the adjective comes after the noun and changes to match it.

examples.es: un café con leche, por favor

items.note: Feminine: la infusión. The accent marks the stress.
Takes el, like el agua: el agua con gas.
Feminine: la horchata. A thick cold drink of rice and cinnamon.

drills.note: Limonada is feminine, so una limonada.
Agua keeps el even though it is feminine.
